text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU capacity exhaustion detected on cluster-gpu-prod. Autoscaling not responding. Symptoms: sustained GPU utilization ~99%, inference request queue ~4k, HPA using external metric `inference_queue_length` not scaling. Runbook reference: /runbooks/gpu-autoscale.md

incident-bot: Paging @Alex (sre-oncall), @Mira (eng-runtime), @Samir (ml-infra). Please ack.

Alex: acked. Escalating to P1. Any infra deploys recently? Who touched prometheus or metrics-adapter in last hour?

Mira: No deploys from runtime. Metrics-adapter logs show repeated 503s when querying Prometheus: 
```
E0310 02:14:10.456 adapter.go:139] error fetching external metric \"inference_queue_length\": prometheus request failed (503)
E0310 02:14:11.780 adapter.go:150] upstream timeout
```
Prometheus UI indicates scrape_lag ~3m for exporters and inference exporter. Node metrics look healthy.

Samir: Prom alert firing: PROMETHEUS_SCRAPE_LAG_HIGH. Prometheus instance experiencing long GC and remote_write backpressure; compaction may be causing pauses. Immediate options: scale Prometheus replicas, restart metrics-adapter, add CPU fallback to HPA, and consider adding temporary GPU nodes.

Alex: Running quick impact: traffic shows ~55% of generation requests returning 429 throttles, ~35% queued >5s, ~10% timing out. Affected customers: alpha-inc (prod), beta-ai (staging->prod), internal-sandbox. Olga, should we inform customers now?

Olga: Yes. I'll post a short status: \"We're investigating increased latency and throttling on inference. Engineers are mitigating. No data loss reported.\" Will follow up with details after mitigation steps.

Mira: Kicking off manual mitigations now:
- restart metrics-adapter deployment
- temporarily set inference deployment replicas to 8
- scale Prometheus statefulset to 3 replicas
Commands: 
```
kubectl -n infra rollout restart deployment/metrics-adapter
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-deployment --replicas=8
kubectl -n monitoring scale statefulset/prometheus-main --replicas=3
```

Alex: Also requesting cloud nodepool resize: nodepool-gpu-prod +4 GPUs. Initiating in cloud console.

ops-bot: autoscaler request accepted: nodepool-gpu-prod resize +4 by Alex. op-id: op-c9f2.

Samir: Reminder: if HPA depends exclusively on external metric and the adapter is down, HPA will not increase pods. Patch suggestion to add CPU resource metric as fallback: 
```
kubectl -n inference patch hpa inference-hpa --type='json' -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/metrics/1","value":{"type":"Resource","resource":{"name":"cpu","target":{"type":"Utilization","averageUtilization":60}}}}]'
```
This will ensure pods scale based on CPU if external metric is unavailable.

Alex: Applying HPA patch now. kubectl output: 
```
horizontalpodautoscaler.autoscaling/inference-hpa patched
```
HPA updated with CPU fallback.

Mira: Restarted metrics-adapter. Adapter logs now show successful responses and external_metrics endpoint healthy. Prometheus scrape lag coming down to ~20s.

Mira: Prometheus replica scaling is progressing. I'm also temporarily reducing retention windows to relieve compaction pressure.

ops-bot: nodepool-gpu-prod scaled: 4 nodes added successfully (gpu-pool-21..24).

Alex: After nodepool scale plus HPA patch and adapter restart, inference queue dropped from ~4k to ~700 over ~18 minutes. Throttles decreased from ~55% to ~15%. Still seeing errors on very long-context requests.

Samir: Good. Recommend routing low-priority tenants to fallback endpoints to reduce load. We should mark beta-ai and sandbox as low-priority and shift traffic.

Mira: Updating routing rules now to redirect low-priority tags to hosted-fallback-model. Applied canary; metrics show immediate relief in queue and pod CPU.

Olga: Alpha-inc wants ETA. Alex, what do we tell them?

Alex: Tell them: engineers are restoring capacity and expect throttles to normalize within 60 minutes. No lost requests; client SDKs will retry. We'll update hourly.

ops-bot: Alert cleared: PROMETHEUS_SCRAPE_LAG_HIGH resolved.

Mira: Follow-ups: verify Prometheus retention/compaction settings, investigate remote_write latency to long-term storage, add stronger autoscaling safeguards. We'll run a postmortem.

Samir: I'll open infra tickets: 1) add liveness/readiness probes on metrics-adapter, 2) implement synthetic external metric for inference_queue_length so HPA can detect adapter failures, 3) add alert for queue >1000 and lower HPA polling interval.

Alex: Handoff to Jonah for overnight monitoring. Handoff summary: \"metrics-adapter -> prometheus scrape lag caused HPA to stop scaling; GPU pool exhausted leading to queue growth and throttling. Actions: restarted adapter, scaled prometheus, added +4 GPUs, patched HPA to include CPU fallback, routed low-priority traffic away. Current state: queue ~200-300, throttles ~5-10%, adapter healthy, prometheus stable. Monitor for 4h.\"

Jonah: Ack. I'll watch for regression and escalate to P1 if queue >500.

Olga: I'll continue hourly customer updates until fully recovered.

Alex: Thanks team. Creating postmortem and scheduling a 1hr follow-up tomorrow. Incident marked mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem ticket INC-20260310-82 created.

incident-bot: Incident state changed to mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem owner: Alex.

[end of thread]
